tasks.short: Assess the disease risk and decide on quarantine, set up quarantine with staff, take samples for testing, request lab tests, record the results, decide whether the disease must be reported, and report it to the authority.

steps.what: Veterinarian assesses the disease risk and decides on quarantine
Veterinarian establishes quarantine procedures with staff and owners
Veterinarian fills paper lab request forms with animal and owner details
Veterinarian reads lab results from e-mail and types them into the record
Veterinarian checks the results against government regulations and decides whether to report
Veterinarian reports the notifiable disease to the authority on its portal

tasks.design: Lab tests are ordered from the practice system ({OTHER}) with animal and owner details filled in, and results come back into the record through the lab's link instead of by e-mail. Deciding on quarantine, setting it up with staff and owners, taking samples and reporting a notifiable disease to the authority stay with the veterinarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lab forms were filled by hand and results retyped from e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Veterinary labs take electronic orders and return results to practice systems.
tasks.still_hard: Owners do not always keep to quarantine rules.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading a farmer to keep animals in when it costs money.

evidence.claim: Veterinary labs can take electronic orders and return results to practice systems.

assumptions: Boundary: from the suspected disease to the disease reported; the authority's measures are outside.
Input contract: the lab offers an electronic link; fallback is paper forms and e-mail.
Quarantine decisions and reporting stay with the veterinarian.
research_questions: Do results reach the record sooner?

incremental.description: Veterinarian checks that results arrived for every request.

approvals.approved_version: The report decision as made by the veterinarian in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few lab tests per case; high: herd testing with many samples.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search literature and surveillance reports on diseases animals could be susceptible to, read the key sources, judge the risk for the animals in care, write the findings into the practice protocols, and share them with colleagues.

steps.what: Veterinarian searches literature and surveillance reports to research diseases animals could be susceptible to

loop.input: The veterinarian's question and an index of veterinary literature and surveillance reports.
loop.output: A short summary of what the sources say, with a citation per sentence.
loop.check: Code checks every citation points to a source in the index and the quoted passage appears in it; sentences without a valid citation are dropped; the veterinarian reads the cited sources.
loop.stop: One summary per question; if no sentence passes the check, the veterinarian searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions are in free text and sources use varied terms; a keyword search returns too many papers to read.

steps.what: Veterinarian judges the disease risk for the animals in the practice's care
Veterinarian writes the findings into the practice protocols
Veterinarian e-mails the findings to colleagues

tasks.design: A bounded step searches an index of veterinary literature and surveillance reports and drafts a short summary with a citation per sentence; code checks every citation exists and the quoted passage is in the source, and drops the rest. The veterinarian reads the key sources and judges the risk. Findings go into the practice's shared protocol library ({DOCS}) in a fixed format, and once written colleagues are notified of the change. Judging the risk stays with the veterinarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Searching papers and reports by keyword took long and gave too many hits.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models summarise indexed sources with citations that code can check.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which farms in the area are at risk.
tasks.altitude: The veterinarian reads checked summaries and key sources instead of searching.

evidence.claim: Language models can summarise indexed sources with citations that code can check against the source text.

assumptions: Boundary: from the disease question to colleagues informed; treatment is outside.
Input contract: the practice has access to an indexed literature collection; fallback is searching by hand.
Reading key sources and judging risk do not change.
No client or animal data go into the search.
research_questions: How often does the check drop a sentence?

incremental.description: Veterinarian reports missing sources for the index.

approvals.approved_version: The protocol note as written by the veterinarian in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new diseases with few sources; high: known diseases with many papers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design the test protocol, treat animals with drug therapies, antibiotics or surgical techniques and observe the effects, record observations, analyse the results, and judge the effect.

steps.what: Veterinarian designs the protocol for testing the drug therapy or surgical technique
Veterinarian treats animals with drug therapies, antibiotics or new surgical techniques and observes the effects
Veterinarian records observations on paper sheets and copies them into a spreadsheet
Veterinarian analyses the results in a spreadsheet
Veterinarian judges the effect of the therapy

tasks.design: Observations are entered on a tablet in a study form per animal and time point in an electronic lab notebook ({DATA_PLATFORM}), so paper sheets are not copied into spreadsheets. The analysis set in the protocol runs as a fixed script on the recorded data, so tables are not rebuilt by hand. Designing the protocol, treating animals and judging the effect stay with the veterinarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations were written on paper and analysed in hand-built spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic lab notebooks take tablet entry; analysis scripts run on study data.
tasks.still_hard: Animal studies are small and effects are noisy.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing an animal in distress and stopping its part of the test.

reach.learn: Whether records are complete and timely.

evidence.claim: Electronic lab notebooks take tablet entry and analysis scripts can run on recorded study data.
Animal tests in the Netherlands need a project licence under the Experiments on Animals Act, with an animal welfare body overseeing them.

assumptions: Boundary: from the study question to the effect judged; the licence application is outside.
Input contract: study forms set up per protocol; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Treating and observing animals do not change.
The analysis plan is fixed in the protocol before the study.

incremental.description: Veterinarian sets up the study form and analysis script per protocol.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small studies with few observations; high: long studies with many time points.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The veterinarian keeps deciding on quarantine, judging disease risk and running animal tests; retyped lab results, keyword searches and spreadsheet copying shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A veterinarian with more time for animals and owners.
